data.name: Gorakhnath
data.long_meaning: Gorakhnath is a revered deity in Hindu mythology, known as the Lord of the Gora (hills) or the one who resides in the mountains. He is considered a form of Lord Shiva and is often depicted as a wandering ascetic, carrying a jhola (bag), a trident, and a Gopalashtaka (a text on Lord Krishna).
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes spiritual enlightenment, detachment, and the pursuit of knowledge in seclusion.
data.numerology_meaning: Creative, expressive, and energetic individuals who excel in artistic and social areas.

data.cultural_impact: Gorakhnath is an essential part of the cultural heritage of various regions, including but not limited to North and Central India. His temple complexes are renowned for their unique architectural styles, vivid festivities, and spiritual practices. One of the most famous shrines dedicated to Gorakhnath is located in the city of Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh, India, which is known for its historical significance and attracts thousands of devotees every year.
data.spiritual_significance: Gorakhnath is believed to represent the spiritual path of self-realization, detachment, and abandoning material possessions. He is a symbol of spiritual renunciation and serves as an inspiration for individuals seeking to purify their minds and strengthen their connection with the divine. Gorakhnath is also known as the Adi-Guru or the first guru, representing the cognitive power and innate wisdom within every individual.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Gorakhnath is mentioned in the ancient Hindu text, the Mahabharata. The name Gorakhnath carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
